title: DEVAI framework repository threat model
subject: aarusso-nyx/devai, the framework repository governed by its own harness under law/policy/self-dogfood.json

boundaries.name: Authority broker
boundaries.inside: A human session that declared exactly one constitutional role and invokes a registered action with explicit write consent.
boundaries.outside: Ambient environment state, undeclared or inferred roles, host tools writing governed paths outside the runtime, and any caller presenting authorization bytes it did not earn.
assets: Governed write paths under law/, product/, packages/, tests/, docs/, record/, .devai/config/, and .devai/pin/
The effect authorization ledger and every one-time Owner grant
The self-dogfood role and effect matrix

threats.description: A caller writes a governed path that its declared role does not own, or relies on a wildcard remainder to widen its scope.
threats.mitigation: Authority is a fixed two-segment path prefix lookup decided before mutation; an unauthorized prefix is refused with zero exemptions.

threats.description: A session infers a role from context, elevates to another role mid-session, or initiates an action reserved to a different discipline.
threats.mitigation: Exactly one declared role per session; ambient state is ignored for authorization and a cross-role action is refused rather than elevated.

threats.description: A remote-write effect replays a consumed authorization, presents a revoked or expired one, substitutes a different candidate or repository, or claims authority by possession of the ledger bytes.
threats.mitigation: Every remote-write consumes exactly one exact, unexpired, unrevoked Owner authorization bound to action, effect, resource, repository, candidate, role, and consent; a gapped, broken, or absent ledger denies everything.

threats.description: A self-dogfood run is triggered by a timer, a hook, or a prior run's output and treats a passing check as publication authority.
threats.mitigation: Self-dogfood invocations are human-initiated, admitted only by the matrix row of the declared role and check id, forbid remote-write for every role, and grant no publication authority.

boundaries.name: Evidence transport
boundaries.inside: Records appended by executing verbs into the hash chain under record/proofs/ and .devai/state/, and the exported evidence bundles bound by content digest.
boundaries.outside: Human edits under record/, evidence rewritten or truncated in transit, credential values that would leak through diagnostics, and any observation that claims a verdict it did not make.
assets: The proof chain and every sensor reading, run, and closure record
Exported evidence manifests and their signatures
Credential values that must never enter a file, a log, or a report

threats.description: A record in the chain is edited, reordered, or removed, or a chain with a gap is resolved to its intact prefix.
threats.mitigation: Evidence is append-only, content-hashed, predecessor-linked, and attributed to the verb; a gap or broken digest link fails verification as a whole.

threats.description: A crash, timeout, missing input, or infrastructure fault is recorded as a PASS or a FAIL, or a BLOCKED probe result is cached and reused as a defect.
threats.mitigation: Every failure is a closed error envelope; an extrinsic failure yields BLOCKED, is never cached as FAIL, and never manufactures a readiness claim.

threats.description: A credential probe, a redacted diagnostic, or a rendered evidence view emits a substring of a secret, or a token shape is committed in configuration.
threats.mitigation: Credential requirements are declared per effect; probes report presence without values, redaction is verified not to leak, and the repository-wide scan fails on any token shape.

threats.description: A reading is recorded without the declaring role or the human invocation, or a second copy of the readings store diverges from the one the scorecard reads.
threats.mitigation: One readings store feeds the scorecard at the same head; a reading without role and invocation is rejected by sense record.

boundaries.name: Release workflow
boundaries.inside: The nine-state release lifecycle executed by the registry role for each action, bound to the canonical repository identity, an exact candidate commit and tree, a plan digest, and the toolchain manifest.
boundaries.outside: Any session, adapter, or workflow step that supplies lifecycle identity, authority, or consent from the client side, a near-match repository or candidate, an unpinned action or runtime, and a publication observed without a verified signed receipt.
assets: The release lifecycle state head and append log
Package tarballs, manifests, SBOMs, and export closures
The published package identity and the trust identity that signs it
The pinned toolchain and the trusted verifier package

threats.description: A release action is invoked by a role other than the one the registry declares, or accepts client-supplied lifecycle identity, digest, actor, authority, authorization, or consent.
threats.mitigation: Each lifecycle action accepts only its declared initiator and its declared locator projection; the core rechecks every bound identity and hashes the only appendable record.

threats.description: A plan, request, candidate, or adapter binding names a repository or candidate that merely resembles the canonical one, or a resume observation claims published without a verified signed publication receipt.
threats.mitigation: Repository locator, candidate commit and tree, plan digest, and trust identity must agree exactly across request, state, store, receipt, and provider; a near match is a mismatch and an unverifiable receipt is no evidence.

threats.description: A workflow pins a node version, action digest, or verifier commit that differs from the toolchain manifest, or a host toolchain mismatch is treated as a silent cache miss.
threats.mitigation: One toolchain manifest is the source of every pin; the workflow check fails by name and value and a host mismatch is a BLOCKED probe.

threats.description: A pure read such as release plan, offline-verify, resume, or status writes state, evidence, or a receipt, or a publication is dispatched from a second grant that was never issued.
threats.mitigation: Pure reads leave the repository byte-identical; every publication consumes exactly one fresh Owner authorization and a consumed one is never replayed.

out_of_scope: Compromise of the host operating system or of the git binary the runtime shells out to.
Compromise of the package registry or of GitHub itself; the workflow defends what it sends, not the receiving service.
Edits made directly to the repository outside the DEVAI runtime by a human with push rights; Article 6 requires the framework to report that boundary, not to control it.
